1.text_clean:
1. The sides of a square are measured to be $5.0 \pm 0.2$ cm. Which of the following gives the area of the square and its uncertainty?
A. $25.0 \pm 0.2\ \text{cm}^2$
B. $25.0 \pm 0.4\ \text{cm}^2$
C. $25 \pm 2\ \text{cm}^2$
D. $25 \pm 4\ \text{cm}^2$

2.text_clean:
2. Two identical balls are dropped at the same time. Ball A is dropped from a height $h$ and ball B from a height $2h$. Air resistance is negligible.
What is the ratio $\dfrac{\text{time for B to hit the ground}}{\text{time for A to hit the ground}}$?
A. $2$
B. $\sqrt{2}$
C. $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$
D. $\dfrac{1}{2}$

3.text_clean:
3. A model plane flies with constant velocity at constant height. Which diagram represents the forces acting on the plane?
[Diagram: four force diagrams A-D of a model plane with vertical (up/down) and horizontal (forward/backward) force arrows of differing relative lengths; in D the opposing vertical arrows are equal and the opposing horizontal arrows are equal]
A. [unequal forces]
B. [unequal forces]
C. [unequal forces]
D. [balanced forces]

4.text_clean:
4. A force which increases uniformly from 0 to a maximum value of $F$ is applied to an object. The object does not move until the force exceeds $0.5F$. As the force increases from $0.5F$ to $F$ the object moves a distance $x$ in the direction of the force. What is the work done by this force?
A. $0.25Fx$
B. $0.5Fx$
C. $0.75Fx$
D. $Fx$

5.text_clean:
5. A body moves with uniform speed around a circle of radius $r$. The period of the motion is $T$. What is the speed of the body?
A. $\dfrac{2\pi r}{T}$
B. $\dfrac{2\pi T}{r}$
C. Zero
D. $\dfrac{\pi r^2}{T}$

6.text_clean:
6. Which of the following is true about boiling and evaporation?
| | Boiling | Evaporation |
A. | occurs throughout liquid | occurs at liquid surface
B. | occurs throughout liquid | occurs throughout liquid
C. | occurs at liquid surface | occurs at liquid surface
D. | occurs at liquid surface | occurs throughout liquid

7.text_clean:
7. A solid of mass $m$ is initially at temperature $\Delta T$ below its melting point. The solid has specific heat capacity $c$ and specific latent heat of fusion $L$. How much thermal energy must be transferred to the solid in order to melt it completely?
A. $mL + mc$
B. $mc + mL\Delta T$
C. $mc\Delta T + L\Delta T$
D. $mc\Delta T + mL$

8.text_clean:
8. The graph shows the variation of pressure $P$ with volume $V$ of an ideal gas during a thermodynamic cycle.
[Graph: P-V cycle; X (high P, low V) to Y along a curve (expansion), Y to Z at constant pressure (compression), Z to X at constant volume (pressure increase)]
During which stages is work done on the gas and work done by the gas?
| | Work done on gas | Work done by gas |
A. | X→Y only | Y→Z only
B. | X→Y and Z→X | Y→Z only
C. | Y→Z only | Z→X and X→Y
D. | Y→Z only | X→Y only

9.text_clean:
9. A piece of ice melts at constant temperature. Which of the following gives the correct change in the entropy of the water molecules and that of the surroundings?
| | entropy of water molecules | entropy of surroundings |
A. | increases | decreases
B. | decreases | decreases
C. | increases | increases
D. | decreases | increases

10.text_clean:
10. For a body undergoing simple harmonic motion the velocity and acceleration are
A. always in the same direction.
B. always in opposite directions.
C. in the same direction for a quarter of the period.
D. in the same direction for half the period.

11.text_clean:
11. Which graph of displacement $x$ against time $t$ represents the motion of a critically damped body?
[Graphs of x against t: A. x falls from initial value to zero quickly and stays at zero without oscillating; B. x decreases slowly, still well above zero at end of graph; C. undamped oscillation of constant amplitude; D. oscillation with decreasing amplitude]

12.text_clean:
12. Which of the following relates the amplitude $A$ of a travelling wave to the intensity $I$?
A. $A \propto I^{-1}$
B. $A \propto I^{-\frac{1}{2}}$
C. $A \propto I^{\frac{1}{2}}$
D. $A \propto I^{2}$

13.text_clean:
13. The diagrams show four different organ pipes drawn to scale. Standing waves in the fundamental (first harmonic) mode are set up inside each pipe. Which pipe produces a fundamental note with the lowest frequency?
[Diagram: A. short pipe open at both ends; B. short pipe closed at one end; C. long pipe (twice the length) closed at one end; D. long pipe open at both ends]

14.text_clean:
14. An ambulance emits a sound of frequency $f$ as it travels along a straight road between stationary observers A and B.
[Diagram: ambulance moving to the right, away from observer A (on the left) and towards observer B (on the right)]
Which of the following shows how the frequency of the sound heard by each observer compares with $f$?
| | Observer A | Observer B |
A. | greater than $f$ | greater than $f$
B. | greater than $f$ | less than $f$
C. | less than $f$ | greater than $f$
D. | less than $f$ | less than $f$

15.text_clean:
15. The intensity distribution of monochromatic light passing through a narrow slit and then incident on a screen is shown below.
[Graph: single-slit intensity against position on screen, central maximum with small secondary maxima on each side]
When the slit width is reduced which diagram shows the new intensity distribution? Diagrams are drawn to the same scale as the original.
[Graphs: A. narrower, same-height central maximum; B. wider, lower central maximum; C. same width, lower central maximum; D. same width, taller central maximum]

16.text_clean:
16. Two polarizing filters are set up so the transmitted light is at a maximum intensity.
[Diagram: light passing through polarizer 1 then polarizer 2; transmitted light emerges]
Through which angle should polarizer 2 be rotated so that no light is transmitted?
A. $45^\circ$
B. $60^\circ$
C. $90^\circ$
D. $180^\circ$

17.text_clean:
17. A resistor X of resistance $R$ is made of wire of length $L$ and cross-sectional area $A$. Resistor Y is made of the same material but has a length $4L$ and a cross-sectional area $2A$. X and Y are connected in series. What is the total resistance of the combination?
A. $1.5R$
B. $2R$
C. $3R$
D. $9R$

18.text_clean:
18. Each of the resistors in the circuit has a resistance of $2.0\ \Omega$. The cell has an emf of $3.0$ V and negligible internal resistance. The ammeter has negligible resistance.
[Circuit: 3.0 V cell connected across two parallel branches: one branch of three resistors in series; the other branch of one resistor in series with ammeter A]
What is the ammeter reading?
A. 0.4 A
B. 0.5 A
C. 1.5 A
D. 2.0 A

19.text_clean:
19. Which diagram represents the pattern of electric field lines of two small positive point charges held at the positions shown?
[Diagrams A-D: A. lines running from one + charge to the other; B. lines pointing outward from both charges, bending away from each other with a neutral region between; C. same shape as B but arrows pointing inward; D. radial outward lines from each charge drawn independently]

20.text_clean:
20. An electron of mass $m_e$ and charge $e$ accelerates between two plates separated by a distance $s$ in a vacuum. The potential difference between the plates is $V$.
[Diagram: two parallel horizontal plates separated by s; top plate at +V, bottom plate at 0]
What is the acceleration of the electron?
A. $\dfrac{m_e eV}{s}$
B. $\dfrac{m_e V}{es}$
C. $\dfrac{eV}{m_e s}$
D. $\dfrac{V}{m_e es}$

21.text_clean:
21. A ball is thrown from the top of a cliff. The initial magnitude of the velocity of the ball at time $t=0$ is $V$. The ball hits the sea at time $t=T$. Air resistance is negligible.
[Diagram: person on cliff throws ball upwards at an angle; parabolic path of ball down to the sea]
Which graph shows how the vertical component of the velocity $v$ of the ball varies with $t$ as it falls to the sea?
[Graphs of v against t from 0 to T: A. straight line starting at V, crossing zero, ending negative; B. straight line from V decreasing to zero at T; C. line starting below V, shallow slope, slightly negative at T; D. line starting below V, crossing zero, ending well below zero at T]

22.text_clean:
22. A satellite is in orbit about Earth at a distance $r$ from the centre of Earth. The gravitational potential energy of the satellite is $E_P$ and its kinetic energy is $E_K$. The radius of Earth is $R_E$. Which graph shows how both $E_P$ and $E_K$ vary with $r$?
[Graphs of E against r: A. starting at $R_E$, $E_K$ positive decreasing towards zero, $E_P$ negative rising towards zero with larger magnitude than $E_K$; B. same shapes but starting at r = 0; C. $E_P$ positive and $E_K$ negative from $R_E$; D. $E_K$ positive with larger magnitude than $E_P$ from $R_E$]

23.text_clean:
23. The graph shows the variation with distance $r$ of the electric potential $V$ for a positively charged hollow sphere of radius $R$.
[Graph: V constant from 0 to R, then decreasing as 1/r beyond R]
Which graph shows how the magnitude of the electric field $E$ varies with $r$?
[Graphs: A. E zero up to R, jumps to maximum at R then decreases; B. E constant up to R then decreases; C. E increases linearly to R then decreases; D. E constant up to R then decreases (different scale)]

24.text_clean:
24. An emf of maximum value $\varepsilon$ is induced in a coil for a particular rate of change of flux. What will be the maximum emf induced in a coil of the same area but with twice the number of turns when the rate of change of flux is reduced by a factor of four?
A. $2\varepsilon$
B. $\dfrac{\varepsilon}{2}$
C. $\dfrac{\varepsilon}{4}$
D. $\dfrac{\varepsilon}{8}$

25.text_clean:
25. A metal rod M is falling vertically within a horizontal magnetic field. The metal rod and magnetic field are directed into the paper. What is the direction of the initial force acting on the metal rod that is predicted by Lenz's law?
[Diagram: rod M (into page) with direction of motion downwards; arrows from M: A. left, B. up, C. right, D. down]

26.text_clean:
26. In a particular atom, the nucleon number is the total number of
A. protons.
B. neutrons.
C. electrons.
D. protons and neutrons.

27.text_clean:
27. The nuclear reaction represented by
$^{1}_{0}\text{n} + ^{235}_{92}\text{U} \rightarrow ^{141}_{56}\text{Ba} + ^{92}_{36}\text{Kr} + 3\,^{1}_{0}\text{n}$
is an example of
A. nuclear fusion.
B. nuclear fission.
C. artificial transmutation.
D. radioactive decay.

28.text_clean:
28. When the cathode of a photoelectric cell is illuminated with red light, a photoelectric current is produced in the cell. The illumination is changed to blue light but the rate at which photons arrive at the cathode remains the same. Which of the following statements is/are correct under these conditions?
I. The number of electrons released is unchanged
II. The current falls to zero
III. The kinetic energy of the electron increases
A. I only
B. III only
C. I and II only
D. I and III only

29.text_clean:
29. The diagram shows the three lowest energy levels of an atom.
[Diagram: three energy levels, increasing energy upwards; top level X, middle level closer to X than to the lowest level]
Which diagram shows the emission line spectrum associated with electron transitions from energy level X?
[Spectra with increasing $\lambda$ to the right: A. two close lines at short wavelength and one line at long wavelength; B. one line at short wavelength and two close lines at long wavelength; C. two lines, one short and one long wavelength; D. three equally spaced lines]

30.text_clean:
30. In the Heisenberg uncertainty principle, conjugate quantities are pairs of quantities that cannot both be known precisely at the same instant. What unit is used for the product of the conjugate quantities?
A. $\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-3}$
B. $\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-2}$
C. $\text{kg m}^2\text{s}^{-1}$
D. $\text{kg m}^2\text{s}$

31.text_clean:
31. In a Bainbridge mass spectrometer, which of the following gives the type of fields used for ion speed selection and ion deflection?
| | Ion speed selection | Ion deflection |
A. | electric field only | electric field only
B. | electric and magnetic field | electric field only
C. | electric field only | magnetic field only
D. | electric and magnetic field | magnetic field only

32.text_clean:
32. Uranium-238 ($^{238}_{92}\text{U}$) forms a nucleus of plutonium-239 ($^{239}_{94}\text{Pu}$) as a result of
A. electron capture followed by alpha decay.
B. electron capture followed by beta decay.
C. neutron capture followed by alpha decay.
D. neutron capture followed by two beta decays.

33.text_clean:
33. The decay constant is the probability of the
A. number of radioactive decays per unit time.
B. decay of a nucleus per unit time.
C. decay of a nucleus.
D. number of nuclei decaying in any given time.

34.text_clean:
34. In the production of electric power, an advantage of using photovoltaic cells rather than fossil fuels is that the photovoltaic cells
A. can be effective in any location.
B. can be used continuously.
C. have low initial set-up costs.
D. are more environmentally friendly when in use.

35.text_clean:
35. A metal sphere X of radius $R$ has an equilibrium surface temperature $T$. Another sphere Y made of the same metal has a radius $\dfrac{R}{2}$ and an equilibrium surface temperature $2T$. What is the value of the ratio shown below?
$\dfrac{\text{power emitted by Y}}{\text{power emitted by X}}$
A. 8
B. 4
C. 0.5
D. 0.25

36.text_clean:
36. A liquid has a coefficient of volume expansion of $1 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{K}^{-1}$. What is the percentage decrease in volume of the liquid when the temperature drops by 20 K?
A. 0.02
B. 0.2
C. 2
D. 20

A. Decommission nuclear power plants
B. Replace the use of coal and oil with natural gas
C. Use combined heating and power (CHP) systems
D. Use hybrid motor vehicles

38. What is the 5-bit binary form of the decimal number 23?
A. 10111
B. 11101
C. 11110
D. 01000

39.text_clean:
39. Capacitance of a capacitor is defined as the
A. ability to store electrical charge.
B. ratio of charge stored to potential difference.
C. ratio of potential difference to charge stored.
D. ratio of work done to charged stored.

40.text_clean:
40. For every 12 photons incident on a pixel of a particular charge-coupled device (CCD), 8 photoelectrons are emitted. What is the quantum efficiency of the pixel?
A. 33 %
B. 67 %
C. 96 %
D. 150 %
